ideas.label: Greek Gift
ideas.summary: The Greek Gift is a bishop sacrifice on h7 or h2 designed to drag the castled king out and bring the queen and knight into a mating attack. Its soundness depends on access routes, not on the sacrifice alone.

ideas.label: Greek Gift
ideas.summary: Before sacrificing on h7, verify that the knight can reach g5 with tempo, the queen can enter on h5 or the h-file, and the defending king cannot escape comfortably through g6, f6, or g8.

ideas.label: Greek Gift
ideas.summary: The sacrifice is stronger when the defender on f6 is absent, pinned, or unable to control h7 and g4, while the attacking side has a stable center. If the center can be opened against your own king, the combination may be too slow.

ideas.label: Greek Gift
ideas.summary: After the king accepts the Greek Gift, calculate forcing moves in order: knight checks, queen checks, and captures that remove flight squares. A quiet move is justified only if it creates an unavoidable threat and the king has no simplifying defense.
